grades: High school juniors and seniors when you apply
name: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP), Gaithersburg
org: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
what_you_do: Spend seven summer weeks in a NIST lab on the Gaithersburg campus. You work with staff scientists and engineers on your own research project and may show it at a poster session.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens who are a high school junior or senior at the time of application, with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must be able to do the full seven weeks and live within 50 miles of the host campus. Families must provide their own housing and transportation.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a competitive volunteer program.
duration: Seven weeks, mid-June to early August (2027 dates to be decided)
deadline_text: Not open yet. The page says the 2027 job announcement is expected on USAJOBS in mid-October 2026, with applications due at the end of January 2027. A lower line says applications generally open Nov 1 and close in the last week of January, so the open date is not firm.
how_to_apply: Watch for the SHIP job announcement on USAJOBS and follow the application page linked from the SHIP page. The page says to read the application process page for the full steps.
notes: The page lists two NIST campuses (Boulder, CO and Gaithersburg, MD); this card is for Gaithersburg. The 2026 poster session was held in Gaithersburg on Aug 6, 2026. The exact application dates for 2027 were not final on the page read, so check it again in late October.
